chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Said from Safwan from Musa ibn Bakr from Zurara from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him)
That the inheritance of the child of li'an belongs to the mother; and if the mother is not alive, then it belongs to the closest people to the mother, her maternal uncles.

key_terms.وَلَدِ اَللِّعَانِ: child of li'an (child resulting from the ritual of conjugal imprecation)

ai.seo_question: Who inherits from a child of li'an if the mother is deceased?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the specific inheritance distribution for the child of li'an, prioritizing the mother as the primary heir. If the mother is deceased, the inheritance devolves to her maternal uncles (akhwal), reflecting the Shia juristic view that the maternal line takes precedence in this unique case over the paternal line due to the absence of a recognized father. This ruling underscores the distinct legal status of the child in li'an, where the father is known but the maternal bond is the primary vehicle for inheritance.
